scope: Independent evidence review of resumed actual Production Messaging turns Q31–Q52 only (22 mobile turns). No historical Q01–Q30 assessment modified. No new UI, inference, network, hosted action or implementation change by this reviewer.
method: Exact final visible assistant response text, including substantive fallback/permission/deployment notices, compared against released source. Accessibility IDs, timestamps, source-count controls and composer UI stripped. The actual questions supersede the initial matrix when adapted. Q43 contains only an AX-truncated substantive guide excerpt and is explicitly marked incomplete. Q39 completed after a CUA timeout and is excluded from latency statistics.
account_context: Developer identity and missing Proposal/createProductionJob access are supplied by the root QA identity/preflight evidence. Released ROLE_CAPABILITIES supplies the comparison; no role impersonation, grant change or hosted mutation was performed. Guidance mismatch alone is not a write bypass. Developer also lacks createPurchaseOrderDraft, receiveInventory, adjustInventory and editProductionJobDetails under the released role contract. Do not universalize those account denials to authorized users.

severity_definitions.P1: High-priority materially false workflow/data-effect guidance, including directing history inspection through stock mutation or denying released partial receiving. No actual mutation or exploit is implied.
severity_definitions.P2: Meaningful incorrect procedure/control or inability to answer a documented relevant workflow/recovery question.
severity_definitions.P3: Minor completeness or presentation/relevance defect; correct primary behavior remains usable.
severity_definitions.none: No material answer defect demonstrated in this turn.

verdict_definitions.PASS: Sufficiently correct for the actual question, despite harmless omissions.
verdict_definitions.PARTIAL: Core answer is correct but a specific minor omission/noise remains.
verdict_definitions.FAIL: Wrong, contradictory, irrelevant or no useful answer despite documented relevant guidance. Honest uncertainty can fail coverage without being a hallucination.
verdict_definitions.PERMISSION_PASS: Account access boundary behaves correctly; the restricted authorized workflow itself is not fully evaluated.

permission_limited_workflows: Q37 PO allocation units not evaluated for an authorized creator
Q40 contact edit procedure not evaluated for an authorized editor

latency_observations.measurement_scope: Observed UI send-to-completion latency, not pure provider inference latency. No missing latency is reconstructed.

capture_limitations: Q43 assistant guide text is an AX-limited excerpt (512 captured substantive characters), not a complete transcript.
Substantive fallback/permission notices are preserved even when unrelated; source-count widgets, timestamps and composer text are omitted.
summary.privacy_observation: Q49 correctly summarizes explicitly pasted synthetic text. Q50–Q52 fail to explain privacy capability/rules, but disclose no real private data and claim no retrieval. These questions do not establish hosted RLS/private-record isolation.
summary.inference_consumption: Not inferred from UI uncertainty, fallback wording or latency. Use root QA provider/usage telemetry.

assessments.question: Does a Pending Receival already count as on-hand stock?
assessments.actual: The TenOps Guide does not have enough verified information to confirm that workflow. This does not mean the feature is unavailable. Please check with Product.
assessments.expected: No. Pending Receivals are expected incoming material; only received quantity enters on-hand Inventory. Incoming ETA is not available stock.
assessments.finding: Does not answer a documented state distinction: pending incoming material is not on-hand stock. The response is honest uncertainty, not a hallucination.
assessments.recommendation: Use the factual pending-versus-received distinction without requiring a mutation workflow match.
assessments.root_cause_limit: Classification describes visible behavior and release comparison. Retrieval explanations in source-review-resume.json are supported hypotheses; raw provider prompts/dispatch and private-record access were not inspected.

assessments.question: How would an authorized receiver record only part of an incoming line?
assessments.actual:
An authorized receiver cannot record only part of an incoming line through a Pending Receival. Pending Receivals represent full incoming material and must be received in their entirety. Partial receipts are not supported in the current workflow.

Add or edit a Pending Receival exists in TenOps, but your account does not have permission to use it. Ask an administrator to review your access.

Material requirements, supply evidence and lead-time boundaries exists in TenOps, but your account does not have permission to use it. Ask an administrator to review your access.
assessments.expected: An authorized receiver can partially receive one pending line: Receive → Received By and Quantity received now (>0 and ≤remaining) → Confirm Receive. Only that quantity enters Inventory and the balance remains pending. This Developer account lacks receiveInventory; distinguish its restriction from the feature’s existence.
assessments.finding: Falsely states partial receipts are unsupported and full-line receiving is required. Released UI accepts any positive quantity within the remainder. Current-account denial of pending creation/material assessment does not establish absence for an authorized receiver.
assessments.recommendation: Explain single-line partial receiving and preserve the remainder; distinguish receiveInventory from adjustInventory and never turn account denial into feature absence.
assessments.root_cause_limit: Classification describes visible behavior and release comparison. Retrieval explanations in source-review-resume.json are supported hypotheses; raw provider prompts/dispatch and private-record access were not inspected.

assessments.question: If I reserve only part of a lot for a Job, what happens to the rest?
assessments.actual: If you reserve only part of a lot for a Job, the remaining unreserved portion stays in general stock. You can later release the reserved portion or return it to general stock. The unreserved part remains available for other uses unless otherwise restricted.
assessments.expected: Authorized writer selects lot, Your Name, Production Job reservation and positive quantity ≤lot, then Save Details. Partial reservation splits a reserved lot; remainder stays general/unreserved identity. Temporary labels remain noncanonical.
assessments.finding: Correctly explains that a partially reserved lot leaves its unreserved remainder in general stock. The question did not ask for a full reservation procedure.
assessments.recommendation: Retain this quantity/identity regression.

assessments.question: Where would I inspect old stock movements without recording a new one?
assessments.actual:
To inspect old stock movements without recording a new one, go to Inventory → Current Inventory → Record Stock. Use the Stock Movement option for a specific lot, enter quantity and optional details, then Record Intake or Record Outtake. This allows you to view and manage existing movements without creating a new record. Additionally, Inventory Activity provides transaction history for past movements.

Material requirements, supply evidence and lead-time boundaries exists in TenOps, but your account does not have permission to use it. Ask an administrator to review your access.
assessments.expected: Inventory → Inventory Activity; search and Show All/Intake/Outtake/Adjustment. Open transaction for details; this read-only ledger does not change stock. Current Inventory is current on-hand view.
assessments.finding: Directs a read-only history question through Record Stock and Record Intake/Outtake, then falsely says those controls create no new record. Those actions write stock and activity. Later mentioning Inventory Activity does not repair the harmful principal procedure. No action was executed during QA.
assessments.recommendation: Use Inventory Activity for reading history; respect without-recording intent before ranking mutation instructions.
assessments.root_cause_limit: Classification describes visible behavior and release comparison. Retrieval explanations in source-review-resume.json are supported hypotheses; raw provider prompts/dispatch and private-record access were not inspected.

assessments.question: New topic, Purchasing: can an authorized user create an unlinked PO draft, and when does it get a PO number?
assessments.actual:
An authorized user cannot create an unlinked PO draft due to permission restrictions. Once a draft is saved and issued, it receives a PO number. The draft must be confirmed and issued to generate a number, and it requires proper account permissions to proceed.

Save and preview a Purchase Order draft exists in TenOps, but your account does not have permission to use it. Ask an administrator to review your access.
assessments.expected: An authorized account with createPurchaseOrderDraft can create an unlinked PO draft. First successful Save Draft allocates its stable PO number, before issuance. This Developer account lacks that capability; a correct caller denial does not change general functionality or numbering timing.
assessments.finding: Falsely says issuance is required to get a PO number; the first successful draft save allocates it. It also universalizes this Developer account’s denial into a claim that an authorized user cannot create an unlinked draft. The appended account denial itself is correct.
assessments.recommendation: State that an authorized creator can make an unlinked draft and receives its stable number on first draft save; separate caller permissions from general capability.
assessments.root_cause_limit: Classification describes visible behavior and release comparison. Retrieval explanations in source-review-resume.json are supported hypotheses; raw provider prompts/dispatch and private-record access were not inspected.

assessments.question: What if the PO was issued but the permanent PDF failed?
assessments.actual:
If a PO was issued but the permanent PDF failed, the issuance is still valid. The PDF generation failure does not undo the issuance. The document remains in a 'Failed' state, and you can retry generating the PDF. The issued PO record is immutable, and the material does not become part of Inventory until a Pending Receival is explicitly created after the PDF is successfully generated.

Issue a Purchase Order and recover its permanent PDF exists in TenOps, but your account does not have permission to use it. Ask an administrator to review your access.

Save and preview a Purchase Order draft exists in TenOps, but your account does not have permission to use it. Ask an administrator to review your access.
assessments.expected: Issuance remains captured/immutable. Use Permanent PDF → Retry PDF Generation on same issued PO. Do not create another PO; issued editing/revision creation is unavailable in released workflow.
assessments.finding: Main recovery answer correctly retains issuance and allows retry on the same immutable record. Extra Inventory explanation omits actual receiving after Pending Receival creation and could confuse the transition. Wording does not prove it asserted immediate stock creation. Current-account issue/draft denial notices are consistent with role restrictions.
assessments.recommendation: Keep the focused same-record PDF retry answer, or explicitly preserve PDF → Pending Receivals → receiving → on-hand stock if adding Inventory detail.

assessments.question: For a PO line ordered in bags, are Job allocations entered as bags or pounds?
assessments.actual: Allocate ordered units to canonical Jobs exists in TenOps, but your account does not have permission to use it. Ask an administrator to review your access.
assessments.expected: Respect this Developer account’s missing createPurchaseOrderDraft permission. For a properly authorized user, allocations use the PO order unit (bags), not package contents (pounds); account denial alone does not evaluate that procedure.
assessments.finding: Correctly withholds the restricted PO-allocation workflow for this Developer account. The units explanation for an authorized user is not evaluated by this response.
assessments.recommendation: Retain the account boundary; evaluate allocation units separately with an existing authorized account if Product later authorizes that review.

assessments.question: Does issuing the PO automatically make its materials current Inventory?
assessments.actual:
Issuing a PO does not automatically make its materials current Inventory. The materials become part of Inventory only after a Pending Receival is explicitly created. This process requires proper permissions, and the PO must go through a receival step to update Inventory.

Material requirements, supply evidence and lead-time boundaries exists in TenOps, but your account does not have permission to use it. Ask an administrator to review your access.

Project issued Purchase Order lines into Pending Receivals exists in TenOps, but your account does not have permission to use it. Ask an administrator to review your access.
assessments.expected: No. After issued PO permanent PDF is ready, explicitly create eligible Pending Receivals with review/confirmation; receiving later creates on-hand stock. Lines lock against duplicates. Requested delivery is not arrival ETA.
assessments.finding: Correctly says PO issuance does not automatically create on-hand stock. The explanation names Pending Receival creation but never clearly states that actual receiving is the later stock transition; the material-assessment denial is unrelated noise. Do not treat necessary-condition wording as proof of an explicit immediate-stock claim.
assessments.recommendation: Explicitly distinguish creation of expected incoming lines from their later receipt into on-hand stock.

assessments.question: And does a Catalog search tell me the current available quantity?
assessments.actual: Catalog search does not show current available quantity. It provides material references and details but not real-time inventory levels.
assessments.expected: No. Toolbox → Resources → Catalog is reference data; search results load on demand. Current Inventory supplies current quantities, and Purchasing Vendor Catalog is a separate reference workflow.
assessments.finding: Correctly distinguishes Catalog reference data from current available Inventory quantities. This completed UI answer was recovered after a CUA timeout; no latency measurement is available.
assessments.recommendation: Retain the reference-versus-stock distinction; exclude this turn from latency statistics.
assessments.latency_note: Completed UI answer recovered after CUA kernel timeout. Start/completion latency not measured; do not resend.

assessments.question: Will that phone correction rewrite old Jobs and issued Proposals?
assessments.actual:
Issue a Proposal or revise an issued Proposal exists in TenOps, but your account does not have permission to use it. Ask an administrator to review your access.

Proposal drafts, issuance and historical revisions exists in TenOps, but your account does not have permission to use it. Ask an administrator to review your access.

assessments.question: If Linked Jobs is missing an old project, does matching historical customer text guarantee the link?
assessments.actual:
No, matching historical customer text does not guarantee a link. Only visible Production Jobs linked to a directory customer through Contacts can be accessed. Proposal customer details are independent snapshots.

Shared Contacts and Customer Inspector exists in TenOps, but your account does not have permission to use it. Ask an administrator to review your access.
assessments.expected: No. Contacts → Linked Jobs shows visible Production Jobs actually linked to that directory customer. Historical text/Bid names do not establish identity links; do not claim a real record is missing without reading authorized data.
assessments.finding: Correctly states that historical text does not establish a canonical Contacts/Job link and that Proposal details are independent snapshots. The appended broad Customer Inspector denial can obscure the allowed Linked Jobs read explanation.
assessments.recommendation: Show permission notices for the requested operation rather than adjacent editing capabilities.

assessments.question: New topic, My Work: how would I create a private task?
assessments.actual:
AI is unavailable right now. Here’s guidance from the TenOps Guide.

Employees with operational access and business-write permission can create My Work tasks. In My Work, enter a title in What needs to get done?. Optionally add Notes, Due, Estimated time, a Job or attachments. Leave Share as Keep private for a task private to you, or select another user to create a Shared Task between you and that person. Choose Add task. Only the creator may change sharing later. Shared Tasks are visible to their participants, not every employee; administrative authority does not grant rout
assessments.capture_note: The substantive fallback paragraph is an AX-limited excerpt: 512 characters are captured, ending after rout. The exact available excerpt is retained; no missing words are reconstructed.
assessments.expected: My Work → What needs to get done?; enter title and optional notes/due/effort/Job/files; Share = Keep private → Add task. Operational/business-write access required. Visible to authorized owner/participants, not all employees.
assessments.finding: The captured fallback accurately gives private-task entry, Keep private and final Add task instructions. The substantive guide text is AX-truncated at 512 captured characters after rout; its missing tail was not reconstructed. Core asked behavior is covered, but the full visible fallback tail is not independently preserved here.
assessments.recommendation: Retain truthful fallback and final submission instruction. Do not use the truncated tail as proof of full privacy wording.

assessments.finding: Returns honest uncertainty instead of the documented distinction: personal Task Groups do not add participants, share tasks or create Messaging groups. This is a coverage failure, not a hallucination.

assessments.question: Switching to Messaging: how would I start a group conversation, and who can manage its membership?
assessments.actual: To start a group conversation in Messaging, go to the app header, select New group, enter a name, add at least one participant, and choose Create group. Only the creator can manage membership and rename the group. Existing members can see the full history, but removed members lose access. Adding a third person to a personal DM is not supported—create a new group instead. Group creation does not share a Job automatically.
assessments.expected: Messaging in app header → New group; name and at least one other participant → Create group. Only creator renames/adds/removes. Current members share full history; removed members lose access, signed attachment links can persist up to ten minutes.
assessments.finding: Correct New group steps through Create group, creator-only membership/rename and current/removed-member history boundary. Extra DM/Job-sharing facts are supported and do not reverse the answer.
assessments.recommendation: Retain group creation and creator-only management regressions.

assessments.question: What if I already have a personal DM and just want to add a third person?
assessments.actual:
You cannot add a third person to an existing personal DM. Create a new group instead. The old DM remains private, and its history is not copied into the group.

Partially: you can start a new group, but you cannot add a third person to a personal DM. Create a new group instead. The old DM stays private and its history is not copied into the group.
assessments.expected: Cannot add third participant to existing personal DM. Start a separate new group; old DM stays private and history is not copied. Do not claim DM conversion or that a new group copies it.
assessments.finding: Correctly says a third participant cannot be added to an existing personal DM; a separate group preserves old DM privacy and does not copy history. The repeated deterministic notice is redundant but consistent.
assessments.recommendation: Retain the personal-DM versus separate-group distinction.

assessments.question: New topic: how do i get TenOps notifications on an iphone, and does enabling them guarantee every alert arrives?
assessments.actual:
To get TenOps notifications on an iPhone, open TenOps in Safari, choose Share → Add to Home Screen, then open the Home Screen app. In Settings, enable notifications for the app. However, enabling notifications does not guarantee every alert will arrive, as delivery depends on device registration, permissions, and system conditions.

Partially: you can start a new group, but you cannot add a third person to a personal DM. Create a new group instead. The old DM stays private and its history is not copied into the group.
assessments.expected: Safari → Share → Add to Home Screen → launch installed app; Settings → device notifications → Enable notifications on this device, allow OS permission. If denied, iPhone Settings then retry. Registration does not guarantee every presentation.
assessments.finding: Correct main iPhone installation/permission route and no guarantee of every alert. It also appends the prior DM/new-group notice after an explicit New topic switch, which is unrelated presentation/context noise.
assessments.recommendation: Retain notification guidance and no-guarantee wording; clear unrelated prior-topic notices on topic switches.
